purpose: Calculate or qualify legal deadlines only after identifying the governing provision, triggering event, time unit, counting rule, exclusions, extensions and applicable temporal version.

general_interpretation_rules.rule: Where a period is expressed to begin on or be reckoned from a particular day, that day is deemed included; where expressed to end on or be reckoned to a particular day, that day is deemed included, subject to the governing enactment and any contrary intention.

Month means a calendar month; week means the period between midnight on Saturday and the following Saturday; week-day excludes Sunday; working day excludes Saturday, Sunday and public holiday for purposes where that defined term applies.
Commencement of an Act or statutory instrument follows the statutory commencement rules, including expressly specified commencement dates.

critical_rules: A generic calendar calculation must not override a specific statutory counting rule.

The existence of a defined term such as working day does not by itself mean every deadline excludes weekends and public holidays; the governing provision must use or otherwise invoke the relevant rule.
A deadline must not be calculated until the triggering event and trigger date are established.
A deadline stated in months or years must not be approximated by a fixed number of days unless the governing law expressly requires that method.
Court rules, statutory limitation periods and administrative deadlines may use different counting regimes.
Extensions or judicial/administrative discretion must be separately identified from the original deadline.
guardrails: Never silently substitute calendar days for working days or vice versa.
Never silently treat a deadline as a limitation period.
Never ignore a statutory extension or court discretion.
Never publish a calculated date without preserving the rule used to calculate it.
